## liboqs

### Round 3 algorithm inclusion

Rodrigo walked through all four round 3 algorithms currently being worked on, and noted with satisfaction that, in late September, every one of them now has an effort underway.

**SDitH (Owen).** Most of the work is done. The remaining sticking point is shimming AES from the upstream implementation over to the OQS symmetric primitives. Owen expects to open the PR today, even though the shim is not yet as clean as he would like, specifically so he can get a second pair of eyes on the approach. Rodrigo had taken a quick look and found the structure very much in line with what he had in mind for the integration.

**QR-UOV ([PR #2582](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/liboqs/pull/2582), [issue #2454](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/liboqs/issues/2454)).** The QR-UOV team joins next week's status meeting, and will be the first submission team to arrive with an inclusion PR already open. Rodrigo noted the unusual amount of community interest in QR-UOV — several people have been working on it — and said he is curious to ask the team why. In its first form the PR duplicated the implementation across all 30 QR-UOV variants, because QR-UOV can only compile one variant at a time and selects it by compile-time macro; the result was roughly 3,000 files to review. Rodrigo asked the implementers to factor the common code into one place, which they have done, and the PR is now much more manageable. Work continues on the reference/AVX2 implementation split, but it is going in the right direction.

**SQIsign (Basil).** Basil was not present, but is making good progress; Rodrigo expects something to look at in the next couple of weeks.

**FAEST (Norm).** Norm made an initial commit to the upstream FAEST repository for the OQS integration points, and the FAEST team accepted it, so that is now in place. The remaining blocker is AES-192 support, [PR #2571](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/liboqs/pull/2571) (for [issue #2570](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/liboqs/issues/2570)), which Norm deliberately kept separate from the FAEST code since it is foundational and independent. He asked for a couple of reviews on it. Once it lands he will open the draft PR for FAEST itself; the underlying work is already done, and what remains is establishing agreement on the shape of the integration. No date is yet confirmed for the FAEST team to join a status meeting.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action (Owen):** Open the SDitH PR and request review specifically of the AES shim approach.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action (reviewers):** Review [PR #2571](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/liboqs/pull/2571) (AES-192 support), which is foundational for FAEST inclusion.

Michael also noted that an active contributor had said they would join today's call to meet the team, but did not appear; he hopes to meet them at the next call.

**liboqs-Python.** Douglas reported a security report that he is working through with the reporter. An environment variable used in the installation routine was not shell-escaped, so someone with control over the environment variables at install time could cause unexpected behaviour — which already presupposes strong access. Douglas assessed it as low, or arguably not a security issue at all, but was eventually persuaded to rate it moderate. A fix is ready and he is waiting for the reporter to confirm that it addresses what they observed. Michael agreed it did not sound serious and was content to leave the assessment as it stands.

## Release planning: liboqs 0.17 and patch releases

Owen relayed a point Bruce had asked to be raised: whether the pace of round 3 inclusion warrants planning a 0.17 release, and how a pending fix should be delivered.

**0.17 scope and timing.** Rodrigo said he had been thinking along the same lines. His original, optimistic expectation was to have all round 3 algorithms in by the end of the year and release then; the actual pace has been faster. His view is that once all four round 3 algorithms are in — possibly as soon as October — that should itself trigger a release, so the round 3 support can be announced as soon as possible. Since the current 0.17 milestone holds a large number of other items (mostly carried over from 0.16), he proposed narrowing the 0.17 milestone to the round 3 algorithms, letting anything else that happens to be ready come along, and moving the remainder to a new 0.18 milestone. Michael, Douglas and Norm agreed. Norm added that the only other consideration would be a significant security finding that ought to ship with the release; he does not think the stateful signature items rise to that level.

**Patch releases.** Owen also asked whether there is a precedent or policy for a patch release, since Bruce had a fix — believed to relate to the CROSS signature scheme — and wondered how to get it out. Rodrigo did not think it warranted an interim release: liboqs is not a production library, so patch releases make little sense in general, and CROSS in particular did not advance to round 3, making it an unlikely candidate to patch. Douglas noted that OQS last did a patch release with 0.10.1 in 2024, plus some in the 0.9 series, and that the project has not maintained parallel release branches; doing patch releases well would require better branch discipline than OQS currently has. Michael agreed, adding that the project's version-numbering discipline itself has been sound — sub-major versions for new algorithms, patch-level for functional and security updates — and that since OQS only supports the latest release for security fixes, there is no need to change the procedure. Douglas clarified that his concern was about parallel development branches rather than version numbering, and agreed on both points.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action (Rodrigo):** Rescope the liboqs 0.17 milestone to the round 3 algorithms and create a 0.18 milestone for the remaining items.
